a.title: NHWA Dataset (linking and indexing, built on CDE-HWR) (Data Object)

text.tspan: NHWA Dataset (linking and indexing, built on
HWR vs NHWA (proposed). The Health Workforce Registry is the system of record: it
creates and maintains only the core data elements (CDE-HWR): demographics, unique
ID/index, licensure, registration, educational credential, organizational
affiliation and facility association. The National Health Workforce Accounts are
not a second registry: they build on CDE-HWR, using the HWR identifier to link and
index records held in other data systems, and compile the NHWA indicators.
Other NHWA data sources (not modelled here, no new actors): education
and accreditation systems, HR and payroll, regulatory council
registers, labour force surveys and census. Modules 3 and 4 draw on
ministries of health, finance, education and labour, payroll and
IFMIS, not the registry (NHWA handbook 2023). They reach the
Reporting Module through the DPI-F Information Mediator, keyed on the

g.text: Key
Colour: which part of the architecture a box belongs to
Why: who cares (stakeholders), and the drivers, goals, outcomes, values and requirements
Strategy: what the organisation is able to do (capabilities) and with what (resources, value streams)
Software: systems and their parts, the services they offer, and the data they hold
Shape: what kind of thing a box is (its small italic label names the exact kind)
Cut corners: a reason or aim, such as a stakeholder, goal, outcome or value
Rounded corners: something done or an ability, such as a capability, process or function
Rounded ends: a service, offered for others to use
Square corners: something that exists, such as a system, a role, or a piece of data
Other marks
A box inside another box: a part of it
Grey band: a grouping for layout only; it adds no meaning
Note: a comment from the authors
Line: how two boxes are related, read from where the line starts to where it ends
Realization: makes real, or achieves
Assignment: is assigned to, or carries out
Aggregation: groups (the end is a part that can also exist on its own)
Access: reads or writes data (the arrow shows which way the data goes)
Flow: passes something, such as information, to
Influence: influences, or contributes to
Association: is related to (no more specific meaning)
